result.topic_en: Gauss's table of primes of the form 8n+7, with their classes of quadratic forms (the 'Classes' with indices and associated powers of 2), preceded by a header table of primes grouped by a number (3, 9, 15, 21, 27, 33, 39, 45).

methods.what: Classification of primes p ≡ 7 (mod 8) by class structure, listing classes and associated powers of 2 with factors
Relation: number of indices is always odd, and (number of indices + 1) = 2 × number of classes
methods.quote: Indicum numerus semper impar, unitate auctus dat bis numerum Classium ut facile demonstr.

methods.what: Primes of form 8n+7 admit no decomposition into squares
methods.quote: Hic nullae discerptiones in quadrata locum habere possunt.

items.quote: Hic nullae discerptiones in quadrata locum habere possunt.
items.english: Here no decompositions into squares can take place.

items.quote: Numerus Classium potest esse cuiusvis formae.
items.english: The number of classes can be of any form.

items.quote: Indicum numerus semper impar, unitate auctus dat bis numerum Classium ut facile demonstr.
items.english: The number of indices is always odd; increased by one it gives twice the number of classes, as is easily demonstrated.
